ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Sick Visit — Irène Joliot-Curie

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for nausea, vomiting and constipation during cycle 1

text.paragraph: Nausea, two episodes of vomiting, and no bowel movement for four days. [S]

Mrs. Joliot-Curie called this morning and was seen the same day, on day 11 of her first cycle of azacitidine with venetoclax. For three days she has felt queasy for most of the day, and she vomited twice yesterday, about an hour after her evening meal; the venetoclax tablets had been taken with breakfast and stayed down. She has had no bowel movement for four days and feels bloated, without severe pain. She has checked her temperature twice a day as instructed; the highest was 37.4 °C. She has had no chills, cough, sore throat, mouth sores, painful urination, diarrhea, or rectal pain. Her gums ooze a little when she brushes, and she has new small bruises on her shins. She is drinking about a liter and a half a day. She takes posaconazole, acyclovir, levofloxacin and allopurinol as prescribed. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-08; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Tired but alert; temperature 37.2 °C, pulse 98, blood pressure 106/64, oxygen saturation 97% on room air; weight 52.4 kg, down 1.1 kg
Dry mucous membranes; a few gum petechiae; no ulcers or thrush
Scattered petechiae and small bruises on both shins; injection sites on the abdomen healing
Mildly distended and soft, with active bowel sounds; no tenderness or guarding. No rectal examination while neutropenic
Two months of tiredness, easy bruising and bleeding gums, with pancytopenia and 12 percent blasts on the blood smear; acute leukemia suspected and urgent hematology review booked
S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the bone marrow diagnosis two days later; its timing echoes the documented decline in her health (D).

Acute myeloid leukemia diagnosed on bone marrow biopsy (34 percent myeloblasts), in a physicist with decades of occupational exposure to ionizing radiation; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to her documented leukemia
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis and subtype; the type of her real leukemia is not documented.

Occupational exposure to ionizing radiation over about four decades: X-ray work early in her career, laboratory work with polonium and other radioactive sources, and a laboratory accident in which a sealed polonium source ruptured on her bench about ten years ago
S — Synthetic modern coding of her documented occupational exposure.
Pulmonary tuberculosis in her forties, treated to completion; no symptoms of active disease
S — Synthetic modern coding of her documented tuberculosis; the treatment details are synthetic.

Moderately reduced lung gas transfer (DLCO 58 percent of predicted, FEV1 76 percent) from old tuberculous scarring of the right upper lobe; with performance status 2, it makes her unfit for intensive induction
S — Synthetic finding on pre-treatment testing.
Nausea with vomiting and constipation on day 11 of cycle 1 of azacitidine with venetoclax, without fever, with mild low potassium; managed as an outpatient; resolved
S — Synthetic treatment side effect; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Nausea with vomiting and constipation during cycle 1 (R11.2). Nausea and constipation are common with azacitidine and venetoclax. No fever, a soft non-tender abdomen and normal bowel sounds make obstruction or neutropenic enterocolitis unlikely, but she knows to come in at once for pain or fever. Potassium 3.3 mmol/L after vomiting, magnesium 1.8 mg/dL. On posaconazole and levofloxacin, both of which can lengthen the QT interval, the ECG today shows a QTc of 446 ms, so ondansetron can be used with care. [S]
Ondansetron 4 mg every 8 hours as needed; no other QT-prolonging antiemetic.
Polyethylene glycol 17 g daily and senna two tablets at bedtime; no suppositories or enemas while neutropenic.
Potassium chloride 20 mEq twice daily for three days; recheck with the next blood count.
Small frequent meals; take venetoclax with breakfast as now.

Acute myeloid leukemia, day 11 of cycle 1 (C92.00). Neutrophils 0.1, hemoglobin 7.4 g/dL and platelets 9 x10^3/uL: the expected nadir. Platelets below 10 call for a prophylactic transfusion, and the hemoglobin with tiredness calls for one unit of red cells. No sign of infection. [S]
One unit of irradiated red cells and one dose of irradiated platelets in the infusion unit today.
Continue venetoclax 70 mg daily and the prophylactic medicines.
Fever plan unchanged: 38.0 °C or more means the emergency department at once.
Blood count twice weekly; bone marrow on day 22.

Red Blood Cell Transfusion: 2023 AABB International Guidelines. JAMA 2023 (PMID 37824153) (2023); Kaufman RM, et al. Platelet transfusion: a clinical practice guideline from the AABB. Ann Intern Med 2015 (PMID 25383671) (2015); Hesketh PJ, et al. Antiemetics: ASCO Guideline Update. J Clin Oncol 2020 (PMID 32658626) (2020)

Follow-up: Nurse phone call tomorrow. Blood count and potassium in three days. Bone marrow and review on day 22. Go to the emergency department at once for a temperature of 38.0 °C or more, abdominal pain, bleeding that does not stop, or vomiting that prevents taking her tablets. Next scheduled visit 2026-10-19: day 22 of cycle 1: bone marrow response, transfusion and infection review, and stopping venetoclax for count recovery. [S]
